10y4ujm:192: The efficiency problem of multi-turn linear dialogue for collecting parameters is not that "dialogue" itself is flawed, but that the way options are presented in dialogue is flawed: the Agent asks one at a time, the human answers one at a time. This linear interaction is extremely costly when there are many options. The solution is to separate the ability to "present all options at once" from dialogue and replace it with a structured panel. The panel's value is not "faster", but "letting humans compare all options at a glance before deciding" — this is the highest-quality mode of human decision-making. Dialogue-based collection makes humans forget previous options when there are many.
